A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVG-Text/CrossText2Loc study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. Both end with references and contain no appendices. Referenced supplementary material, including additional evaluations mentioned in v2, is unavailable, limiting comparison of those parts.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, retrieval experiments, text-synthesis and positional-embedding ablations, and multimodal retrieval results in Figures 2–6 and Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds confidence-reranking results, comparator results and an expanded attention analysis.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 extends ERM from providing explanations to producing confidence scores and reranking five candidates using normalized similarity and confidence. This changes inference, but the dual encoder, contrastive objective, positional interpolation and text-generation pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The displayed experiments retain CVG-Text, New York, Brisbane and Tokyo, with satellite/OSM retrieval and image-text queries. v2 newly mentions cross-city evaluation and collaborative satellite/OSM retrieval in unavailable supplementary material. Their settings cannot be inspected to determine whether coverage expanded or existing coverage was evaluated differently.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds X-VLM while retaining all previous baselines. Table 5 adds SAFA, Geo-Dtr and a Text-only comparator to the existing Sample4G and Sample4G + Text comparison; Text-only is newly included in this particular comparison.

E3.justification: Table 5 removes R@5 reporting and adds average R@1 across satellite and OSM retrieval. v2 also specifies explanation-evaluation measures, including CIDEr, ROUGE-L and human scoring, but their supplementary protocols are unavailable. The documented main split, training budget and 100-candidate retrieval setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the with/without-ERM comparison in Table 2 and a text-only control in Table 5. Figure 6 expands the attention analysis from six to eight categories by adding SignName and Direction. The text-synthesis and positional-embedding ablations in Tables 3–4 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new LMM confidence scores are retrieval outputs, not statistical uncertainty estimates for the experimental results.

E6.justification: Existing Table 2 scores are unchanged, with v1's Ours row retained as Ours (w/o ERM). The added reranked method reports New York R@1 of 50.33 for satellite and 62.33 for OSM, versus 46.25 and 59.08 without ERM. New comparator and attention-category results are added, while Table 5 drops R@5 entries. Section 5.2 also changes the claimed 14.8% L@50 improvement to Recall@10, inconsistent with Table 2's metrics.

T1.justification: The positional-interpolation, contrastive-loss and attention-propagation equations remain identical; the first two are merely reordered and renumbered. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The introduction's third contribution now explicitly promises confidence alongside retrieval reasons. The main claims concerning the new task, dataset, long-text retrieval and greater-than-10% recall improvement remain essentially unchanged in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 interprets LMM confidence as a proxy for user decision-making and explains why a high-similarity result can still be unconvincing, motivating reranking or additional user descriptions. Existing interpretations concerning city differences, POI information and Japanese text are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the reranking parameters: five candidates, a stated 0.5 confidence threshold, normalization to [0, 1] and score summation. It also clarifies joint encoder training, training all comparators on CVG-Text, and similarity-score fusion for Sample4G + Text. These latter disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier implementation; hardware, training hyperparameters and access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for AnyLoc, X-VLM, Geo-Dtr, CIDEr and ROUGE, while removing CrossViewDiff, SkyDiffusion, Loki and URBench. These are limited changes to supporting literature; the central positioning against image-based cross-view retrieval and point-cloud language localization remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 presents contrastive learning before positional expansion, and explanation-related material from v1 Sections 5.2 and 5.4 is consolidated into v2 Section 5.3. Local explanations are rewritten and Qi Zhu is added to the author list, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Several central displays are substantially redesigned: Figures 1 and 4 are redrawn, Figure 5 reformats the retained examples with callouts and confidence values, and Figure 6 adds categories and changes its word cloud and placement. Tables 1 and 5 reorganize rows and columns, and Table 2 adds rows and second-best highlighting. Together these constitute a substantial visual revision.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's explanation-only ERM, v2 provides an explicit reranking procedure and a paired evaluation in Table 2. Additional baselines and the text-only control in Table 5 modestly strengthen the empirical comparisons. These benefits outweigh the new Recall@10/L@50 reporting inconsistency, although unavailable supplementary evaluations cannot be credited as verified improvements.
